# Jayamadu Gammune — Robotics & Autonomous Systems Engineer

> Biomedical Engineering graduate (Robotics & Automation, First Class Honours, 2026) from the University of Moratuwa, Sri Lanka. Researcher in autonomous robotic systems, computer vision, GPU-accelerated medical imaging, learning-based control, and embedded systems. Open to PhD and research positions from Fall 2027.

## About

Jayamadu Gammune is a Biomedical Engineering graduate from the University of Moratuwa (Robotics & Automation pathway) with research experience at Swinburne University's Intelligent Robotics Laboratory (Melbourne, Australia) under Assoc. Prof. Mats Isaksson. His work spans GPU-accelerated robotic ultrasound imaging, vision-language models for robotic manipulation, EEG-based brain-computer interfaces, and autonomous embedded systems.

## Research Interests

- Robotics & learning-based control for manipulation
- Soft robotics and novel robotic mechanisms
- Mechatronic system design — UAVs & unmanned vehicles
- Computer vision & deep learning for perception
- Vision-language models for task understanding
- GPU-accelerated medical imaging

## Key Projects

- **RoboBrain 2.0 Extension (2026)**: Extended the CVPR 2025 baseline with an LLM planning layer; 50% memory reduction via 8-bit quantization
- **GPU-Accelerated Robotic Ultrasound (2024–2025, Swinburne)**: Hybrid CPU–GPU point-cloud pipeline achieving a 27% latency reduction; published at MERCon 2026
- **Paediatric EEG-Based BCI (2026)**: SSVEP brain-computer interface with custom low-noise PCBs for a child with locked-in syndrome
- **Survey Drone (ongoing)**: ArduPilot/Pixhawk platform for automated aerial image capture and map reconstruction
- **Autonomous Micromouse (2025)**: STM32-based FloodFill maze-solving robot with custom motor drivers
- **SLRC 2024 Robot**: National robotics competition autonomous mobile robot

## Education

- B.Sc. Engineering (Honours), Biomedical Engineering — Robotics & Automation, University of Moratuwa, Sri Lanka, 2022–2026. First Class Honours, GPA 3.77/4.00.

## Experience

- Intern Research Affiliate, Intelligent Robotics Laboratory, Swinburne University of Technology (2024–2025)
- Visiting Instructor, Dept. of Electronic & Telecommunication Engineering, University of Moratuwa (Sep–Nov 2025: EN 2091)
- Visiting Instructor (Teaching Assistant), same department (Jun–Oct 2026: EN 3563, EN 4594, EN 2091)

## Publications

- D.J.T. Gammune, M.C. Roshan, and M. Isaksson, "Systematic GPU Acceleration for Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound Imaging via Point Cloud Pipeline Optimization," Proc. MERCon 2026. doi:10.1109/MERCon71835.2026.11691436
- D.J.T. Gammune et al., "Development of a Child-Friendly Non-Invasive Brain-Computer Interface for Paediatric Locked-in Syndrome," Proc. 19th Asia Pacific Congress of Paediatrics (APCP 2026), Colombo, Jul. 2026. [Abstract]
